Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

At 6.30 a.m. 20-10-41 Sub-lieut. Katoda accompanied by other members of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters called at Crime Branch Headquarters and requested assistance to conduct raids at :-
1. No. 237 Tatung Road
2. Lane 285, House 8 Shanhaikwan Road
explaining that recently information had been received from several places in the occupied area's to the effect that pictures of an Anti-Japanese nature were being distributed by a company known as the Van Jeu (萬友) Industrial Society, and that as result of his enquiries he had ascertained that such a company had premises at one of the two aforesaid addresses.

Necessary arrangements having been made with the U.S. Marine Corp and Sinza Station the desired assistance was rendered by D.I. Crighton, D.S. Yamakara, D.S.I. Meu Shang Tsai and C.D.S. 40.

On the first address being visited it was ascertained that the Van Jeu Industrial Society, had previously occupied those premises, but about one year ago had moved to House No. 8, Lane 285 Shanhaikwan Road.

This latter address was visited and as result of a search conducted therein several hundred copies of

THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW

Nov. 25, 1939.

The China Motion Picture Company at Chungking, has announced its intention of producing in picture form the book, "Secret Agent of Japan," which was written by Amleto Vespa, an Italian who served for many years as an adviser to Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang in Manchuria and later was forced to serve in a similar capacity with the Japanese. He succeeded in escaping from Manchuria after the beginning of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1937 and came to Shanghai where he wrote his book exposing Japanese atrocities in Manchuria. Mr. Vespa and his wife and children are now in the United States.

Acting on information obtained by U.D.C. 308
Wong Chun Fee that the Chinese edition of an English
publication entitled "Secret Agent of Japan" by
Amleto Vespa was being printed by the Hua Mei Printing
Press (華美印書館), 80 Kuling Road, these premises
were raided by members of the Special Branch during
the forenoon of April 30.
Ying Sin Liang (邢錫良), son of Ying Is Shang
(邢義生), the manager of the concern, and an employee
of the Commercial Press, who was present during the
raid, was instructed to cease printing of the book in
question which was immediately complied with.
On subsequent interrogation at Police Headquarters
Ying declared that the concern was printing 3,000 copies
of the book (of approximately 200 pages) on behalf of
the Publication Department of the News Digest, 160
Avenue Edward VII, at a cost of $300.00 which covers
the expenses of printing only, the paper for same being
supplied by the News Digest. Approximately nine-tenths
of the printing had been completed and the greater part
of which had been sent to the Chen Sin Kee (陳信記)
Book Binding Shop, House 9, Lane 139, Loong Chin Li
(龍津里), North Chekiang Road, for binding. Regard-
ing the order for printing the book, Ying continued,
the press had a contract with the Publication Depart-
ment of the News Digest which, however, was in the
custody of his father and was not available owing to

During the afternoon of April 17, 1939 members
of the Special Branch visited Room 405, 210 Kiukiang
Road, where books of an anti-Japanese propaganda
nature were alleged to be on sale.

The premises proved to be the offices of the
"Alexander Publishing and Printing Company." the sole
proprietor of which is Alexander BUCHAN, American of
radical tendencies, details of whom appear in the
attached file.

Enquiries made from Chinese members of this
office - BUCHAN was absent at the time of the visit -
revealed that the concern had been responsible for
printing and publishing an anti-Japanese booklet
entitled "Life or Death Place" ( 生死場 ), several
copies of which were seized by the Special Branch from
various bookstores on Foochow and Shantung Roads on
April 6. No further copies of this publication were
observed in Room 405, 210 Kiukiang Road, the responsible
Chinese staff member declaring that all copies available
had been already despatched to Wenchow. A careful
examination of other literature on the premises revealed
nothing inimical to Japanese interests.

In view of the fact that BUCHMAN is an American
citizen and as the head of the publishing company, solely
responsible for the printing of the booklet "Life or
Death Place," this individual was communicated with
and requested to call upon the P.A. to the D. C.

APPENDIX

(1) Book entitled "Shanghai Day by Day"
Compiled by Chu Tso-doong ( 朱作栋 ) and
Mei Yih ( 梅 益 ).
Issued by the Hwa Mei Publishing Company
(American), 172 Avenue Edward VII.
This book contains for the most part articles
relating to the Sino-Japanese hostilities and
describes the heroic deeds of the Chinese soldiers
and civilians during the period between August 13,
1937 and August 13, 1938. It is actually a diary
of events in the first year of the hostilities
written from a Chinese point of view.

(2) Book entitled "Criticisms on Guerilla Warfare":
Written by General Chu Teh ( 朱德 ), communist
leader and commander of the 8th Route Army.
Published by Chien Zoe (建社) Society,
in November, 1938.
Issued by the "University Press Ltd." (British),
130 Ningpo Road.
This book contains the essential points in
connection with guerilla warfare along political,
economic and military lines against the Japanese.
It also gives an account of the hostilities in which
the 8th Route Army participated against the Japanese
during the past year.

(3) Book entitled "Common Problems on Anti-Japanese
Guerilla Tactics."
Written by General Mao Shih-tung, leader of the
Communist Party.
Published by Chien Zoe Society, on November 30, 1938.
Issued by the "University Press Ltd.",
130 Ningpo Road.

- 2 -

This book gives an analysis of political and
military tactics in the fight against the Japanese.

(4) Book entitled "Life or Death Place":
Written by Siao Hoong ( 萧 三 ).
Published and distributed by the "Alexander
Publishing and Printing Company (American)*,
Room 405, 210 Kiukiang Road.
This book contains cartoons together with
inscriptions describing the resistance made by the
peasants in the North East against the Japanese rule.

(5) Book entitled "Basic Steps for Guerilla Units."
Written by Yue Chi ( 尤 基 ).
Published by Chien Zoe Society (no address),
in December, 1938.
Issued by the "University Press, Ltd",
130 Ningpo Road.
This book describes the principal work and
tactics necessary to be adopted by guerillas and
quotes the experiences of the Red Army of Soviet
Russia during their Revolution. The book is purely
a theoretical work on guerilla warfare and no mention
is made of the Japanese.

(6) Book entitled "Political Work in Guerilla Corps".
Written by Tieh Jen ( 铁 人 ) and
Loo Zeu-ching ( 罗 瑞 卿 ).
Published by Chien Zoe Society, in December, 1938.
Issued by the "University Press Ltd.",
130 Ningpo Road.
This book gives a brief account of political work
among the 8th Route Army and teaches the reader how
to train guerillas in a political sense.

- 3 -

Written by Koh Hwa-shih (郭化若),
Zung Poh-chun (陳伯鈞), and
Seu Yah (水 俠).
Published by Chien Zoe Society.
Issued by the "University Press Ltd.",

This book contains three chapters: one dwells
on the importance of obtaining the assistance of

how to attack the "enemy"; and third teaches the
guerillas how to harass the "enemy" by destroying
communications and to defend themselves against
tanks.
